chunks: Ahmad ibn 'Abdun informed me, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, who said: 'Ali ibn Ya'qub Abu al-Hasan al-Baghdadi narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Isma'il ibn Salih al-Saymari, who said: al-Hasan ibn Rashid narrated to me, who said: Hammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me, who said: Some of our companions narrated it; he mentioned it from al-'Abd al-Salih, Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal, peace be upon him.
He said: Khums is in five things, and khums is divided into six shares.
And he mentioned the detailed explanation of that in a lengthy report which we have cited in our large book, to its end; so whoever wants it may consult it there.

key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: khums, the one-fifth tax discussed as a legal obligation
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ: a title referring to the Imam, peace be upon him
key_terms.خَبَرٍ طَوِيلٍ: a lengthy hadith report containing the fuller discussion
key_terms.خَمْسَةِ أَشْيَاءَ: five categories of things in which khums applies
key_terms.سِتَّةِ أَسْهُمٍ: six shares into which khums is divided

ai.seo_question: How is khums divided according to this hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report states a legal ruling concerning khums: that it applies to five categories of things and that it is apportioned into six shares. The present text is an abbreviated citation that points the reader to a longer narration for the detailed breakdown.
